question: Two circles have radii of 8 cm and 3 cm. The distance between their centers is 15 cm. What is the length of a direct common tangent?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct Common Tangent (DCT) = √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²)

Substitute the given values: d = 15, r₁ = 8, and r₂ = 3 directly.

DCT = √(15² − 5²) = √(225 − 25)

DCT = √200 = 10√2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 10√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of first circle (r₁) = 8 cm

Radius of second circle (r₂) = 3 cm

Distance between centers (d) = 15 cm

 C1 C2 
• d = 15 cm 
• 
• 
• 8 cm 3 cm DCT = ? 

**Formula Used:**

Length of Direct Common Tangent (DCT) = √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²)

**Calculations:**

⇒ DCT = √[15² − (8 − 3)²]

⇒ DCT = √[225 − 5²]

⇒ DCT = √[225 − 25]

⇒ DCT = √200

⇒ DCT = √(100 × 2)

⇒ DCT = 10√2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

The formula for the length of a transverse common tangent is TCT = √(d² − (r₁ + r₂)²).

Number of Common Tangents

If d > r₁ + r₂, the circles do not intersect or touch each other, resulting in a total of 4 common tangents (2 direct, 2 transverse).

When Circles Touch Externally

If d = r₁ + r₂, the circles touch externally at exactly one point. There are 3 common tangents in this case, and the Direct Common Tangent formula directly simplifies to DCT = 2√(r₁ × r₂).
